framePolicy: Before any GitHub query, require every stratum search to declare an explicit size:<N upper bound no greater than 500000 KiB. For each stratum query, take GitHub's first min(repositoryCount, pages*perPage) results in stars-desc order at the order-freeze cutoff; record repositoryCount, retrievedCount, the cap, truncation, and the last retrieved repository. Reject unknown-size and >=500000 KiB rows locally before first-match assignment and hash ranking. Apply each search's declared primaryLanguageEligibility predicate before first-match assignment. Assign every remaining exact repository identity to its first matching stratum before hash ranking. This is a single terminal 200-repository wave: no later-wave membership exists. This experiment reuses the same ordered searches, first-match assignment, structural eligibility, and hash ranking. Allocations are scaled prospectively from the v50 200-repository proportions; no commit-message text is queried.

capacityConstraint.policy: Start at ten times each v50 allocation; cap a stratum at its eligible count in the frozen Stage 0 metadata universe, then redistribute the shortfall by iterative largest-remainder weighting over the original nonzero v50 allocations with spare capacity.
